findings.title: h2 headings render at 3 different sizes
findings.evidence: “Give your organization a memory it can use.” is 48px while “Trusted by organizations managing complex knowledg” is 30px (1.6×). Sizes seen: 30px ×1, 36px ×15, 48px ×1. Same semantic level should get the same treatment.
findings.fix: Pick one size for h2 and set it once in CSS. If one of these is really a sub-heading, change its tag instead of its size.
findings.citation: UICrit: elements at the same level of hierarchy should get similar graphic treatment (Duan et al., UIST '24)

findings.title: h3 headings render at 5 different sizes
findings.evidence: “Clearer view of organizational direction.” is 24px while “FROM” is 14px (1.71×). Sizes seen: 14px ×2, 16px ×11, 18px ×8, 20px ×17, 24px ×2; weights: 400, 500, 600, 700. Same semantic level should get the same treatment.
findings.fix: Pick one size for h3 and set it once in CSS. If one of these is really a sub-heading, change its tag instead of its size.
findings.citation: UICrit: elements at the same level of hierarchy should get similar graphic treatment (Duan et al., UIST '24)

findings.title: Placeholder content still on the page
findings.fix: Replace with real names, real testimonials or nothing. A fake testimonial is worse than none.

findings.title: Text sits too close to its box edge
findings.evidence: div.p-8.rounded-xl: the text is 0/0/0/0px (top/right/bottom/left) from the box edge at 16px text; 4 sides are under 3px.
findings.fix: Give the box at least 8px on every side (about half the font size).

findings.title: Glowing coloured shadows (6)
findings.evidence: div.w-4.h-4: zero-offset 18px blur in rgb(26, 114, 200). Dark background + neon glow is tell #6 in the Reddit corpus and #2 on the Fountain Institute list.
findings.fix: Use neutral elevation shadows (black at low alpha, offset downward). Light should come from somewhere.

findings.title: Links to this page unfurl as a blank card
findings.evidence: No og:image. Every share on iMessage, Discord, Slack, X and LinkedIn renders from these tags.
findings.fix: Add <meta property="og:image"> (1200×630), <meta property="og:title"> and <meta name="description"> with one specific sentence. In Next.js, export `metadata` from the page.

findings.title: Nested cards (×15)
findings.evidence: “Card inside card (div)” · “Card inside card (div)” · “Card inside card (div)”
findings.fix: Cards inside cards create visual noise and excessive depth. Flatten the hierarchy — use spacing, typography, and dividers instead of nesting containers.

findings.title: h4 headings render at 2 different sizes
findings.evidence: “Project Titan: Delay Risk” is 18px while “Q3 Strategic Alignment” is 16px (1.13×). Sizes seen: 16px ×1, 18px ×1. Same semantic level should get the same treatment.
findings.fix: Pick one size for h4 and set it once in CSS. If one of these is really a sub-heading, change its tag instead of its size.
findings.citation: UICrit: elements at the same level of hierarchy should get similar graphic treatment (Duan et al., UIST '24)

findings.title: 22 rounded panels on one page
findings.evidence: Rounded corners on every container is one of the ranked vibe-coded tells (#5 in the Reddit corpus).
findings.fix: Round the things that are interactive or elevated; let sections and layout containers stay square.

findings.title: Inter for 100% of the text
findings.evidence: Primary family is Inter, one of the fonts generated UIs default to. Fonts seen: Inter, ui-monospace.
findings.fix: Not wrong on its own. If everything else is default too, this is the cheapest thing to change: pick one typeface with a point of view for headings and keep the workhorse for body.
findings.citation: Impeccable overused-font; HN thread on vibe-coded tells (Inter everywhere)

findings.title: 1 row of three identical cards
findings.evidence: Three 389px-wide cards of equal weight (“Verified Enterprise”, “Verified Enterprise”, “Verified Enterprise”). The hero + three feature cards skeleton is tell #9; equal weight tells the reader nothing is more important than anything else.
findings.fix: Decide which one matters and make it bigger, or turn the three into one sentence each under a single heading. Break the symmetry once.
findings.citation: vibecoded-design-tells #9; 21st.dev: uniform features is a top-5 tell

findings.title: Eyebrow label above the hero headline
findings.evidence: “Organizational Intelligence Platform” (14px, tracked caps) sits directly above a 72px h1. The tiny label + giant headline pairing is the default generated SaaS hero.
findings.fix: Fold the label into the headline or the first sentence. If it's an announcement, make it a real link somewhere else.

findings.title: 8 untouched shadcn/ui cards
findings.evidence: Class strings like “p-6 rounded-xl border bg-card” are the component library's defaults, unmodified. Fine as scaffolding; as the final look it's tell #1.
findings.fix: Change the tokens (radius, border colour, shadow) once in your theme so the components stop looking like the docs page.

findings.title: Centered hero: big headline, centered sub, centered buttons
findings.evidence: h1 at 72px, centered, with 3 centered blocks under it. On 23.5% of Show HN launches. It's the layout every builder emits when nobody chooses one.
findings.fix: Not a problem on its own, but combined with other tells it's the skeleton. Left-align and put the product next to the headline, or lead with the product itself.

findings.title: 3 tracked all-caps section labels
findings.evidence: Small uppercase, letter-spaced labels like “From” above sections. On 10.5% of Show HN launches, and usually redundant with the heading under them.
findings.fix: Delete the label or fold its word into the heading.

findings.title: Blurred colour blobs behind the content (1)
findings.evidence: div.absolute.inset-0 is a blur(64px) wash. The aurora backdrop is the default "atmosphere" of generated heroes.
findings.fix: Remove it and let the content carry the first screen. If you want atmosphere, use one real image.

findings.title: Head is missing: canonical
findings.evidence: No JSON-LD structured data either, so AI search engines have nothing to cite. One h1, good.
findings.fix: Ten minutes of <head> work: title under 60 chars, canonical URL, lang attribute, favicon, and an Organization or WebSite JSON-LD block.

findings.title: “How it works” in 4 numbered steps
findings.evidence: 4 siblings each lead with a number in a badge. The three-step setup strip was on 9% of Show HN launches; on a landing page it usually says less than one screenshot would.
findings.fix: Replace with the actual product: a screenshot, a 10-second clip, or the real command to run.

findings.title: Stat banner: 01 · 02 · 03 · 04
findings.evidence: A row of 4 big numbers with small labels. On 12% of Show HN launches. Real numbers are fine; the pattern reads as template when the numbers are round, unsourced, or "99.9% uptime" on a weekend project.
findings.fix: Keep it only if each number is real, specific and checkable (link the source). Otherwise fold the one true number into a sentence.
